name: Ragdoll
funFact: Ragdolls tend to go limp and relaxed when picked up, which is how the breed got its name.
healthNote: Ragdolls are sometimes screened for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, a heart condition worth discussing with a vet.
about: Ragdolls were developed in California in the 1960s and are prized for their striking blue eyes and plush semi-long coat. They're famously docile, often following their owners from room to room and settling happily into a lap for hours.
description: A gentle and affectionate breed that enjoys being close to people.

name: Maine Coon
funFact: Maine Coons are one of the largest domesticated cat breeds, with males often reaching 8–9 kg.
healthNote: Maine Coons are commonly screened for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and hip dysplasia given their size.
about: Native to the United States and one of the oldest natural breeds in North America, the Maine Coon is built for cold climates with a shaggy, water-resistant coat and tufted paws. Despite their imposing size, they're known as gentle giants with a playful, dog-like temperament.
description: A large, friendly and playful breed known for its social personality.

name: Siamese
funFact: Siamese cats are famously vocal and will happily hold a conversation with you.
healthNote: Siamese cats can be prone to dental issues and certain respiratory sensitivities, so regular checkups are recommended.
about: One of the oldest and most recognizable Asian cat breeds, the Siamese originated in Thailand (formerly Siam) and became popular worldwide for its striking color-point coat and piercing blue eyes. They form intense bonds with their people and aren't shy about voicing their opinions.
description: A vocal and social breed that loves attention and interaction.

name: Bengal
funFact: Bengals descend from crosses with the Asian leopard cat, which gives them their wild-looking coat.
healthNote: Bengals are sometimes monitored for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and progressive retinal atrophy.
about: Bred by crossing domestic cats with the Asian leopard cat, Bengals carry a wild look with a distinctly domestic temperament. They're highly intelligent and athletic, and often enjoy water, climbing and interactive play more than the average housecat.
description: An energetic and curious breed that loves climbing, exploring and playing.

name: British Shorthair
funFact: Their round face and calm grin are often credited as the inspiration for the Cheshire Cat.
healthNote: This breed can be prone to weight gain, so portion control and regular activity are worth keeping an eye on.
about: A classic English breed with roots tracing back to Roman times, the British Shorthair is known for its dense, plush coat and round, teddy-bear face. They're easygoing and independent, content to relax nearby rather than demand constant attention.
description: A calm and independent breed that enjoys company without demanding constant attention.

name: Sphynx
funFact: Despite having no fur, Sphynx cats still need regular baths to manage oil buildup on their skin.
healthNote: Sphynx cats are sometimes screened for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and need extra care to protect their exposed skin from sunburn and cold.
about: Developed in Canada in the 1960s from a natural hairless mutation, the Sphynx is anything but low-maintenance — their bare skin means they crave warmth, sunlight and close physical contact. They're playful and people-oriented, often described as more dog-like than cat-like.
description: An affectionate and outgoing breed that enjoys warmth, attention and company.

name: Persian
funFact: Their long, thick coat needs daily brushing to prevent mats and tangles.
healthNote: Their flat facial structure can be linked to breathing and eye-tearing issues, and they're sometimes screened for polycystic kidney disease.
about: One of the oldest cat breeds, the Persian has been prized for centuries for its luxurious long coat and sweet, gentle expression. They favor a calm, predictable routine and are happiest curled up in a quiet corner of the home.
description: A quiet and affectionate breed that prefers a calm and comfortable environment.

name: Abyssinian
funFact: One of the oldest known cat breeds, with a look believed to resemble cats depicted in ancient Egyptian art.
healthNote: Abyssinians are sometimes screened for pyruvate kinase deficiency, a hereditary condition affecting red blood cells.
about: With a lineage often linked to ancient Egypt, the Abyssinian has a distinctive ticked coat that gives it a wild, foxlike appearance. They're endlessly curious and athletic, happiest when given plenty of space to climb, explore and investigate.
description: An intelligent and energetic breed that loves exploring and staying active.
